revision.text:
[[File:Taisei Hōkan.jpg|thumb]]
'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|qq=}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|qq=}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
== References == * {{cite journal|和書|author=青山忠正|title=大政奉還後の政治状況と諸藩の動向|year=2017|journal=歴史学部論集|volume=7|pages=131–139}} * {{cite journal|和書|author=高橋秀直|title=王政復古への政治過程|year=2001|journal=史林|volume=84|issue=2|pages=165–201}}
== Related Articles == * [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]] * [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] * [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] * [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]]

His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|qq=}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|qq=}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q709528]] Wikidata name: Taisei Hokan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:42, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:Taisei Hōkan.jpg|thumb]]
'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|qq=|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|qq=|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[commons:Category:Taisei Hokan]][[en:Taisei Hokan]][[fa:بازگشت قدرت سیاسی به امپراتور]][[ja:大政奉還]][[ko:대정봉환]][[ru:Возвращение государственной власти Императору]][[th:ไทเซโฮคัง]][[uk:Повернення державної влади Імператору]][[zh_min_nan:Tāi-chèng hōng-hôan]][[zh_yue:大政奉還]][[zh:大政奉还]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q709528]] Wikidata name: Taisei Hokan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:42, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:Taisei Hōkan.jpg|thumb]]
'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|qq=|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|qq=|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Taisei Hokan]][[en:Taisei Hokan]][[fa:بازگشت قدرت سیاسی به امپراتور]][[ja:大政奉還]][[ko:대정봉환]][[ru:Возвращение государственной власти Императору]][[th:ไทเซโฮคัง]][[uk:Повернення державної влади Імператору]][[zh min nan:Tāi-chèng hōng-hôan]][[zh_yue:大政奉還]][[zh:大政奉还]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q709528]] Wikidata name: Taisei Hokan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:42, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:Taisei Hōkan.jpg|thumb]]
'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|qq=|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|qq=|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Taisei Hokan]][[en:Taisei Hokan]][[fa:بازگشت قدرت سیاسی به امپراتور]][[ja:大政奉還]][[ko:대정봉환]][[ru:Возвращение государственной власти Императору]][[th:ไทเซโฮคัง]][[uk:Повернення державної влади Імператору]][[zh-min-nan:Tāi-chèng hōng-hôan]][[zh-yue:大政奉還]][[zh:大政奉还]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q709528]] Wikidata name: Taisei Hokan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:42, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:Taisei Hōkan.jpg|thumb]]
'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|qq=|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|qq=|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|qq=|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Taisei Hokan]][[en:Taisei Hokan]][[fa:بازگشت قدرت سیاسی به امپراتور]][[ja:大政奉還]][[ko:대정봉환]][[ru:Возвращение государственной власти Императору]][[th:ไทเซโฮคัง]][[uk:Повернення державної влади Імператору]][[zh-min-nan:Tāi-chèng hōng-hôan]][[zh-yue:大政奉還]][[zh:大政奉还]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q709528]] Wikidata name: Taisei Hokan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:42, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:Taisei Hōkan.jpg|thumb]]
'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Taisei Hokan]][[en:Taisei Hokan]][[fa:بازگشت قدرت سیاسی به امپراتور]][[ja:大政奉還]][[ko:대정봉환]][[ru:Возвращение государственной власти Императору]][[th:ไทเซโฮคัง]][[uk:Повернення державної влади Імператору]][[zh-min-nan:Tāi-chèng hōng-hôan]][[zh-yue:大政奉還]][[zh:大政奉还]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q709528]] Wikidata name: Taisei Hokan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:42, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:Taisei Hōkan.jpg|thumb]]
'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[sn:commons:Category:Taisei Hokan]][[en:Taisei Hokan]][[fa:بازگشت قدرت سیاسی به امپراتور]][[ja:大政奉還]][[ko:대정봉환]][[ru:Возвращение государственной власти Императору]][[th:ไทเซโฮคัง]][[uk:Повернення державної влади Імператору]][[zh-min-nan:Tāi-chèng hōng-hôan]][[zh-yue:大政奉還]][[zh:大政奉还]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q709528]] Wikidata name: Taisei Hokan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:42, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:Taisei Hōkan.jpg|thumb]]
'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
== References == * {{cite journal|和書|author=青山忠正|title=大政奉還後の政治状況と諸藩の動向|year=2017|journal=歴史学部論集|volume=7|pages=131–139}} * {{cite journal|和書|author=高橋秀直|title=王政復古への政治過程|year=2001|journal=史林|volume=84|issue=2|pages=165–201}}
== Related Articles == * [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]] * [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] * [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] * [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]]

The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).

The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.

'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].

'''Taisei Hōkan''' (大政奉還) refers to the return of political authority to the Emperor by the 15th Shōgun of the [[:en:Edo Shogunate|Edo Shogunate]], [[:en:Tokugawa Yoshinobu|Tokugawa Yoshinobu]], on {{ill|October 14, 1867|ja|慶応3rd year 10月14日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 14, 1867|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 9, 1867, by the Gregorian calendar). The Emperor [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Meiji]] subsequently approved this act on {{ill|October 15|ja|慶応3rd year 10月15日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 15|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 10, 1867).
== Overview ==
During the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|1=Tokugawa shogunate|2=ja|3=江戸幕府|lt=Tokugawa shogunate|lt=Tokugawa Shogunate|ja|徳川幕府|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Shogunate|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 江戸幕府}} ruled Japan as the de facto governing power, with the justification of the Emperor’s delegation of authority, a theory widely known as the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}}.
By the late Edo period, however, tensions arose between the [[:en:Royal court|Imperial Court (Japan)]] and the Shogunate, particularly over foreign relations, challenging the legitimacy of Shogunal power. During [[:en:Bunkyū|Bunkyū]] and [[:en:Genji era|Genji]] (1863–1864), the Shogunate sought reaffirmation of the delegated authority doctrine. These reaffirmations marked the institutionalization of what had previously been a customary practice.
The {{ill|Taisei Hōkan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan|qq=}} on October 14, 1867, represented the formal return of this authority to the Emperor. However, Tokugawa Yoshinobu did not immediately resign as Shōgun. His resignation was submitted on {{ill|October 24|ja|慶応3rd year 10月24日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 24|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (November 19, 1867), and the Shogunate was officially abolished during the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} on {{ill|December 9|ja|慶応3rd year 12月9日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/December 9|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (January 3, 1868).
The Taisei Hōkan aimed to avoid civil war, reform Shogunal despotism, and establish a {{ill|Kōgi Seitai|ja|公議政体|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōgi Seitai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 公議政体論|1=Kōgi Seitai Ron|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11392219}}, or a consensus-based political system led by the Tokugawa family. However, before the planned assembly of feudal lords could occur, pro-Imperial forces, led by [[:en:Satsuma Domain|Satsuma Domain]], initiated the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
'''Note: All dates are in the {{ill|Japanese lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese lunar calendar|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|qq=}} unless otherwise specified.'''
== Development ==
=== Political Climate and Doctrine of Delegated Authority ===
In the late Edo period, divisions arose over issues such as {{ill|open trade agreements|ja|通商条約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/open trade agreements|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, leading to conflicts between the Imperial Court and Shogunate. Events such as the {{ill|Bunkyū Reform|ja|文久改革|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bunkyū Reform|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 文久の改革|1=Bunkyū Reforms|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11499741}} saw the Shogunate pressing for the institutionalization of the {{ill|Doctrine of Delegated Authority|ja|大政委任論|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Doctrine of Delegated Authority|1=Doctrine of Delegated Authority|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11435592}} to reinforce its power under the guise of Imperial approval.
Simultaneously, thinkers like [[:en:Yokoi Shōnan|Yokoi Shōnan]] and [[:en:Katsu Kaishū|Katsu Kaishū]] proposed the concept of returning political authority (Taisei Hōkan), but these proposals were largely ignored due to the Shogunate's insistence on [[:en:Kōbu gattai|Kōbu Gattai]].
=== The Role of Tosa Domain ===
The [[:en:Tosa Domain|Tosa Domain]] actively promoted Taisei Hōkan. Notably, [[:en:Gotō Shōjirō|Gotō Shōjirō]] and [[:en:Sakamoto Ryōma|Sakamoto Ryōma]] advocated for peaceful political reform. The {{ill|Senchū Hassaku|ja|船中八策|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Senchū Hassaku|1=Senchū hassaku|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q8191633}}, attributed to Ryōma, laid out a framework for such a transition.
After negotiations between Tosa and Satsuma representatives, including the {{ill|Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|ja|薩土盟約|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|1=Satsuma-Tosa Alliance|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11622270}}, Tokugawa Yoshinobu submitted his resignation in response to the Tosa petition.
=== The Submission of Authority ===
On October 14, 1867, Yoshinobu formally submitted the {{ill|Taisei Hōkan petition|ja|大政奉還上奏文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisei Hōkan petition|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to the Imperial Court. After deliberations, it was accepted the following day, with the Court issuing an edict outlining future deliberations on national policy.
Although Yoshinobu relinquished authority, he retained significant influence. It was only after the {{ill|Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja|王政復古の大号令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōsei Fukko no Daigōrei|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 王政復古 (日本)|1=restoration of imperial rule|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q835568}} that his power was decisively curtailed.
== Contents of the Petition == {{see|s:德川內府大政返上ノ奏議}}
The petition emphasized Yoshinobu’s acknowledgment of the need for centralized Imperial authority to navigate foreign and domestic challenges.
== Legacy ==
Taisei Hōkan represented a strategic maneuver to maintain Tokugawa influence within a new Imperial framework. However, its limited scope led to conflict, culminating in the [[:en:Boshin War|Boshin War]].
